title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 1, 2026: Micron Earnings Spark KOSPI Rally
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · Market Close, October 1, 2026

KOSPI closed at 6,971.35, up 1.95%, while KOSDAQ closed at 879.74, up 2.78%, as a blowout Micron earnings report reversed an early slide driven by surging U.S. long-term Treasury yields. Here is what moved the market today.

What moved today

Micron's earnings surprise flips the market from red to a sharp rally

Korean markets opened weak as U.S. long-term Treasury yields pushed above 5%, dragging KOSPI down to roughly 6,765 intraday. The mood reversed after Micron reported its largest-ever quarterly results and pointed to long-term growth in AI server and memory demand, lifting Samsung Electronics and SK hynix into positive territory intraday. KOSPI surged past the 6,900 level to close up 1.95%, while KOSDAQ closed up 2.78% at 879.74 on combined foreign and institutional buying, with semiconductor equipment/materials and pharma-bio names jointly driving the index higher. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Trump names Alaska LNG and 8 new U.S. reactors in Korea energy investment announcement

U.S. President Trump said Korea's planned U.S. energy infrastructure investment includes the Alaska LNG project and construction of eight large nuclear reactors in the U.S., reviving related infrastructure expectations. The U.S. side cited more than $50 billion for Alaska LNG and roughly $120 billion for the reactor project. If the Alaska LNG and reactor projects move forward, they could generate large-scale demand for steel, specialty steel, pipe and construction materials, drawing buying into Daehan Steel, Korea Steel Wire, and Seah Besteel Holdings. However, the only project Korea's government has actually confirmed is a Texas gas-fired combined-cycle power plant; Alaska LNG and the eight reactors remain subject to further negotiation, so today's move is better read as positioning on the announcement rather than a confirmed investment. (Reported)

KOSDAQ strength spreads into pharma and biotech

With KOSDAQ up more than 2% on combined foreign and institutional buying, strong rotational buying spread into small and mid-cap pharma and biotech names. With biotech sentiment already improved since HLB's U.S. FDA approval, expectations around individual clinical trials, drug development, and drug-delivery platforms lifted G2GBio, RGenomics, AbClon, Samchundang Pharm, Aimed Bio, Olix, Qurient, Inventage Lab, Green Cross Wellbeing, ABL Bio, and Hanall Biopharma. Today's biotech strength looks like a combination of improved post-HLB biotech sentiment, individual pipeline momentum, and a broader KOSDAQ risk-on mood rather than one single sector-wide catalyst. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Micron's earnings beat spreads buying across semiconductor equipment and materials

Micron posted record quarterly results that beat market expectations and pointed to long-term growth in AI server and memory demand, sharply improving sentiment toward Korean semiconductors. As Samsung Electronics and SK hynix turned positive intraday, buying spread beyond large caps into inspection/test, front-end, back-end, materials and parts suppliers, including SEMES, QRT, TFE, Dreamtech, STI, Hanyang Digitech, DI Corporation, Jeju Semiconductor, SemiFive, Zeus, FST, Dongjin Semichem, Leeno Industrial, Eugene Technology, Techwing, MK Electron, Koh Young, Qualitas Semiconductor, YC, Wonik IPS, Psytech/Cimax, and Exicon. With AI infrastructure investment expanding and memory prices rising, expectations of improved memory-maker earnings feeding into higher capex and equipment/materials orders are driving a broad re-rating of these supplier names; semiconductor equipment and materials companies have also been taking up a growing share of KOSDAQ's top market-cap names recently. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

MLCC names extend gains on AI server and ESS demand

Demand for high-capacity, high-reliability MLCCs tied to AI server and ESS market growth continues to rise quickly, with supply-shortage concerns adding to the strength in related names. AI servers use far more MLCCs than standard servers; Samsung Electro-Mechanics recently signed a roughly KRW 1.0722 trillion long-term supply agreement for AI-server MLCCs with a major global customer as it rapidly expands its AI-related product mix, and the company projects the AI-server MLCC market to grow more than 30% annually through 2030. As major makers also expand production of higher-margin AI and automotive MLCCs, expectations are building for tighter general-purpose MLCC supply and higher prices; MLCC lead times are reported to have stretched from roughly 8 weeks to as long as 32 weeks. Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Amotech, Hanchem, Kochip, and Samwha Capacitor advanced on the news. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI reverse from a weak open to a sharp gain today?
Rising U.S. long-term Treasury yields pressured the open, but Micron's record quarterly results and improved AI/memory demand expectations lifted Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, driving KOSPI to a 1.95% gain by the close.

Is the Alaska LNG and U.S. reactor investment confirmed?
No. The only confirmed project is a Texas gas-fired power plant; Alaska LNG and the eight reactors remain subject to further negotiation between the two governments.

Why did KOSDAQ outperform KOSPI today?
Combined foreign and institutional buying concentrated heavily in semiconductor equipment/materials and small and mid-cap pharma-bio names, both KOSDAQ-heavy sectors.
